summary: Unpredictable single insert performance due to blocking and excessive indexes.
symptoms: Single record insert taking over 7 minutes.
Blocking session IDs reported by sys.dm_exec_requests but no active blocker found.
Blocked requests waiting for LCK_M_S lock type.
mechanism: Blocking caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks, exacerbated by contention from excessive indexes.

facts.key: Table has 34 indexes despite being an OLTP system.
facts.evidence: Post mentions the table has 34 indexes.
Post explicitly states blocked requests are waiting for LCK_M_S lock type.

facts.key: Blocking session ID reported but no active blocker found.
facts.evidence: Post describes sys.dm_exec_requests showing a blocking session ID but no active query in sys.dm_exec_requests.

facts.key: Insert performance is generally good except for occasional outliers.
facts.evidence: Post mentions that insert performance is usually good.

assumptions: The blocking is caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks.
Excessive indexes contribute to contention during inserts.
unknowns: Impact of other concurrent processes on the blocking behavior.
